criteria: True distance along the road network from centroid to nearest main highways
assumption: Short distance can reduce travel time to transit and increase development business

criteria: Average transit time from site location to CBD or key economic centres
assumption: Estimated travel times can increase chance of land growth

criteria: True distance from the land to major road or branches
assumption: Increases site visibility and commercial traffic exposure

criteria: Cumulative shortest network distance (Closeness / Betweenness) along the street network connecting the site to all other network nodes/intersections
assumption: Sites with lower cumulative network distance to all intersections exhibit higher centrality, making them prime candidates for suburban sub-centers and higher land value appreciation

criteria: Physical roadway characteristics: total number of lanes and right-of-way width
assumption: Wider roads with higher capacity support higher development density and larger project scales

criteria: Distance from the site frontage to the nearest U-turn
assumption: Easier U-turn access directly improves convenience for residential and commercial entrance and exit

criteria: Annual Average Daily Traffic (AADT) or peak-hour passenger car units (PCU) measured along the target road segment from official transport department surveys
assumption: Higher baseline traffic throughput increases site visibility and commercial exposure, driving higher roadside land values and development potential

criteria: Kernel Density Estimation index calculated within local catchment areas
assumption: High taxi standby density provides transit connectivity to main roads

criteria: Spatial surface density of local van hubs and songthaew route terminals
assumption: Greater feeder hub density improves public transport accessibility for suburban residents

criteria: Concentration of fixed bus stops within 500 m - 1 km
assumption: Higher bus stop density enhances commuter convenience and local traffic

criteria: Registered demographic counts within a 1 km to 3 km localized catchment area
assumption: Higher population density creates strong localized housing demand under Hedonic Price theory

criteria: Historical percentage change in population over 5-10 years
assumption: Sustained population growth signals long-term spatial expansion and commercial viability

criteria: Network distance to major commercial hubs, shopping malls, and fresh markets
assumption: Proximity to retail and lifestyle hubs commands premium land pricing

criteria: Network distance to educational institutions and healthcare facilities
assumption: Access to essential public amenities directly influences family home-buyer preferences

criteria: Total physical land area of the target parcel
assumption: Parcel size dictates the maximum allowable gross floor area and project typology

criteria: Total width of the land parcel directly abutting the main road or alley
assumption: Wide frontage allows better architectural layout and higher Floor Area Ratio (FAR) realization

criteria: Baseline starting launch prices of surrounding residential developments
assumption: Existing market prices set the baseline valuation expectations for future launches. Different typologies require distinct minimum plot sizes, frontage widths and yield target rates under Highest and Best Use (HBU) analysis

criteria: Official comprehensive urban planning color codes (e.g., Yellow, Orange, Purple)
assumption: Zoning rules impose non-negotiable statutory limits on allowable real estate typologies

criteria: Floor Area Ratio (FAR) and Open Space Ratio (OSR) regulatory limits
assumption: Higher FAR allowances directly increase the maximum buildable floor area and land yield

criteria: Minimum required setback distance from road centerlines or water bodies
assumption: Setback mandates restrict the buildable footprint of the parcel

criteria: Historical frequency of natural flood occurrences over a 10-year window
assumption: High flood frequency lowers site attractiveness and reduces long-term appreciation

criteria: Maximum recorded inundation depth during peak flood events
assumption: Severe flood risks apply a penalty score reduction on development potential
